title: Hweelonalay
sketch: G: a refrain in no language. The refrain is made only of the noises a mouth makes when it has no words (a whistle, a lull, a call, a hum), so it belongs to every border equally and can never be translated or owned. The verses are charms: rules for carrying the song, and every one ends by setting the words, which perish, against the sound, which stays. Chanted 4/4 in phrygian.

verse_template.note: Every verse is a charm, spoken to whoever carries the song: what to do with it (carry it low, forget its words, hand it to a stranger, let a machine have it, die with your mouth open). Lines 3 and 4 always set the words, which are for once, against the sound, which is for keeping. Plain nouns only: coat, bone, fire, stone, map, hill, window, grave. The refrain is never translated, glossed, or given a meaning; if a verse says what the sounds mean, it is wrong.

hooks.why: the whistle leaping to the high tonic and leaning on the flat second: hwee-lo-na-lay
the cry up to the third and the stall on the high flat second
the fall by leaps onto the hum: hwee-lo-na, hom

seed_verses: Car-ry it low in the back of your throat,
car-ry it all the day long;
words are a coat, and the coat will wear through,
sound is the bone of the song.
Sing it three times with the words that you know,
let them all fall to the earth;
words are the fire, and the fire will go out,
sound is the stone of the hearth.
Give it to some-one who has-n't your tongue,
some-one from o-ver the hill;
words will turn back at the edge of the map,
sound goes wher-ev-er it will.
Let the ma-chine have it, let it go round,
let it go round and a-bout;
words that it sings will be new ev-ery time,
sound is the same com-ing out.
Die if you must, with your mouth left a-jar,
o-pen a win-dow as well;
noth-ing goes in-to the ground but the words,
no-bo-dy bur-ies a spell.
No-bo-dy made it, it came with the breath,
ev-ery-one's breath-ing the same;
words have their mak-ers, and mak-ers have graves,
sound nev-er an-swered a name.
